failure_story: We sized Adobe as a subscription compounder on FY2025 owner cash of $23.07 per share, assuming 9% growth in years 1–5, a 25× exit multiple, and a proof-first component sum of $656 per share versus ~$223 spot—implying 32.0% per year synthesis return. Instead, generative-AI alternatives (Canva, Figma, Midjourney, platform-native tools) eroded Creative Cloud net seat additions faster than embedded Firefly monetization offset, RPO growth lagged revenue for two consecutive quarters, and management flagged competitive seat churn in filings. Digital Media ARPU stalled as individual-tier pricing capped; Experience Cloud enterprise deals slowed with marketing-budget cuts. Owner cash growth in the model overstated reality: trailing free cash flow per share fell toward the contract falsifier below $18.00, buybacks slowed as debt rose to $6.21 billion on a January 2025 $2.0 billion note offering while cash fell to $5.43 billion, and the market re-rated the equity from pricing-power compounder to AI-disrupted legacy software. Moat downgraded from stable to eroding; the selling multiple compressed from 25× toward 15–18×; hold-period return landed near or below the 13.3% bear Lawrence envelope and far below the 32.0% base case—a severe capital loss on a partial-dhando name where equity de-rating, not distress, was the primary loss path.
